name: Builder.io (Fusion, now Builder Code)
product: AI visual development platform (Fusion, renamed Builder Code in Sept 2026) that turns Figma designs and prompts into code inside an existing repo and design system, with a headless CMS (Builder Content).
starting_paid_price: Pro about $24/user/month billed annually or $30 month-to-month (third-party reading of pricing page); extra credits $25 per 500
latest_funding: $67M raise announced with Builder 2.0 (exact date not confirmed, 2026); earlier $20M led by Microsoft M12 (Apr 2024)
founders_or_ceo: Steve Sewell (co-founder and CEO)
africa_use_case: Nigerian and Kenyan product agencies could use Builder Code to turn client Figma files into production React inside their own repos without growing frontend headcount.
notes: Fusion renamed Builder Code and Publish renamed Builder Content on 10 Sept 2026 per awesomic.com; Builder.io says pricing is unchanged. Free plan has 15 daily / 60 monthly agent credits (builder.io/pricing). Pricing skews to teams.

name: Locofy.ai
product: AI tool (Large Design Models) that converts Figma or Penpot designs into frontend code for React, Next.js, React Native, HTML/CSS and other frameworks.
starting_paid_price: Hobby $40/month (Pro $80/month); free plan gives 2,000 LDM tokens with Hobby features for 7 days
latest_funding: Seed II $4.25M led by Northstar Ventures (May 2023), $7.3M total; Accel-backed
founders_or_ceo: Honey Mittal (co-founder and CEO), Sohaib Muhammad (co-founder and CTO)
africa_use_case: Freelance frontend developers in Lagos or Nairobi could convert client Figma screens to React Native code to ship mobile apps faster.
notes: Entry paid plan at $40/month is expensive for individual African developers. ISO 27001 and SOC 2 claims per third-party review.

name: Anima
hq_country: Israel (Tel Aviv, with New York presence)
product: Design-to-code platform and AI Playground that builds editable React or HTML apps from Figma files, prompts, URLs or images, with a Figma plugin, MCP server and API.
starting_paid_price: Starter plan exists but price not shown in fetched page text; Enterprise from $500/month billed annually
latest_funding: Strategic investment from IBM Ventures (Feb 2026); $12.62M raised over 4 rounds; Series A $10M (Sept 2021)
founders_or_ceo: Avishay Cohen (co-founder and CEO), Michal Cohen (CPO), Or Arbel (CTO)
payment_methods: Credit cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay; wire transfer or invoice for Enterprise (Anima pricing FAQ)
africa_use_case: African UI designers could clone a reference site or import a Figma file and publish a working React prototype for a local client in one session.
notes: YC S18. Self-serve checkout is card and wallet based, which fits the card-dependency criterion. Funding detail from Startup Nation Central.

name: Uizard
product: AI UI design and prototyping tool (Autodesigner, screenshot and wireframe scanners) that generates app and web mockups with React and CSS handoff.
starting_paid_price: Pro $12/month billed yearly or $19 monthly
latest_funding: Part of Miro (acquired May/June 2024); about $18.6M raised before acquisition
founders_or_ceo: Tony Beltramelli (co-founder); Mathias leads Miro Prototypes after the acquisition (surname not confirmed)
africa_use_case: Non-technical African founders could sketch an app on paper, scan it into Uizard and get clickable screens plus React/CSS to hand to a developer.
notes: Kept rather than swapped: still sold standalone under its own brand after the Miro acquisition. Borderline AI coding product (mainly design, with code export). Some homepage versions point to Miro Prototypes. Co-founder name from general knowledge of the company, not re-verified in this session.

name: Google Stitch
product: Google Labs experiment that turns prompts, sketches, screenshots or voice into multi-screen UI designs and front-end code (HTML/CSS, Tailwind, Flutter and others) with Figma export.
starting_paid_price: No paid plan; free with a daily credit limit
latest_funding: Part of Alphabet (public company)
founders_or_ceo: Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai (product lead not found)
africa_evidence: Google has African offices and developer programmes, but no source found links them to Stitch.
africa_use_case: African students could prototype app UIs for free and export Flutter code to build on.
notes: No paid plan, so nothing for Cozzipay to collect today. Watch for a paid tier after the Labs phase.

name: Relume
product: AI website builder that generates a sitemap, wireframes and designs from a brief, then hosts the site or exports it to Figma, Webflow or React.
starting_paid_price: Hosting from $12/project/month; Build Pro from $14/month; Site Builder Starter $18/month
latest_funding: Bootstrapped; angel investment at a reported $80M valuation (Feb 2025, AFR)
founders_or_ceo: Dan Anisse (co-founder and CEO), Adam Mura (co-founder and CPO)
africa_use_case: Web design studios in Cape Town or Accra could produce client sitemaps and wireframes in minutes and export to Webflow or React.
notes: support@relume.io published in Relume refund FAQ and community replies. Pricing split into Publish and Export tracks.

name: Framer (AI)
product: Website design and publishing platform with AI page generation and AI agents (since 2026) for building and running marketing sites.
starting_paid_price: Basic $10/month (Pro $30/month), per Oct 2025 pricing update; Scale plan since retired
latest_funding: Series D $100M at $2B valuation led by Meritech and Atomico (Aug 2025)
founders_or_ceo: Koen Bok (co-founder and CEO), Jorn van Dijk (co-founder)
africa_evidence: No evidence found in searches. Framer marketplace has third-party PPP components for customer sites, but Framer itself shows no African pricing.
africa_use_case: African startups could launch and iterate a marketing site on the $10 Basic plan without a developer.
notes: Low entry price and large startup user base make it a good pitch target. Confirm current prices on framer.com/pricing.

name: Webflow (AI)
product: Visual website platform with AI site and app generation, and Source by Webflow (Sept 2026 research preview), where marketing teams and AI agents build sites together.
starting_paid_price: Basic site plan $15/month billed yearly ($25 monthly)
latest_funding: Series C $120M at $4B valuation led by YC Continuity (Mar 2022)
founders_or_ceo: Linda Tong (CEO); founded by Vlad Magdalin, Sergie Magdalin and Bryant Chou
africa_evidence: Webflow lists independent Certified Partner freelancers in South Africa, but this is a directory of independent providers, not an official reseller or office.
africa_use_case: South African and Nigerian agencies already building on Webflow could pay for client site plans through Cozzipay instead of corporate cards.
notes: Founder names from general knowledge, not re-verified in this session. Certified Partner directory pages exist for South Africa and Cape Town.

name: Durable
product: AI website builder for small service businesses that generates a site in about 30 seconds, plus CRM, bookings, invoicing and AI review replies.
starting_paid_price: Launch $25/month or $22/month billed yearly
latest_funding: Series A $14M led by Spark Capital (Dec 2023); $20.25M total
founders_or_ceo: James Clift (founder and CEO)
africa_use_case: Salons, tutors and tradespeople in Lagos or Nairobi could get a booking-ready site and invoicing for a monthly fee paid from mobile money.
notes: Strong SMB fit. Not a code-export tool; it generates hosted sites. CEO name from general knowledge, not re-verified in this session.

name: 10Web
hq_country: United States (Delaware/Newark entity; team in Armenia)
product: AI builder that generates hosted WordPress sites, stores and apps from a prompt, URL, Figma file or social profile, with code editing.
starting_paid_price: AI Starter $10/month billed yearly ($120 first year)
latest_funding: Seed $2M from Sierra Ventures and AI Fund (2020); later rounds not confirmed
founders_or_ceo: Arman Mkrtchyan (founder and CEO)
africa_use_case: African small businesses selling on Instagram could turn their profile into a WordPress store and pay the $10/month plan locally.
notes: One source says AI-built sites cannot leave 10Web hosting. Third-party sources disagree on whether a free plan exists (site generation is free; hosting is paid). CEO name from general knowledge, not re-verified in this session.

name: Hostinger Horizons (AI Builder)
product: Hostinger's AI website and app builder with an agentic mode, code editor and export, bundled with hosting, domains and email.
starting_paid_price: Premium $1.99/month on a 48-month upfront term (renews $10.99); Nigeria: NGN 1,990/month (NGN 95,520 for 48 months)
latest_funding: Private and bootstrapped; 2025 revenue EUR 275.4M (+51%)
founders_or_ceo: Giedrius Zakaitis (CEO, appointed 2026; previously Daugirdas Jankus)
africa_evidence: Hostinger's Nigeria page prices the Horizons AI builder plans in naira. Hostinger officially launched in Nigeria in Dec 2025 with naira payments; the Nigeria checkout accepts naira cards and OPay.
availability_in_africa: Dedicated Nigeria storefront (hostinger.com/ng) with naira pricing since Dec 2025. A fintech blog reports Nigerian cards are still often declined because of CBN foreign-spend limits and region-detection mismatches.
payment_methods: Global site: Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover, JCB, Diners, PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, AliPay, crypto. Nigeria site: naira Visa/Mastercard and OPay (per EverTry blog).
africa_use_case: Kenyan, Ghanaian and other non-Nigerian SMBs, who still pay in USD by card, could fund a multi-year Horizons plan through Cozzipay.
notes: Already localized in Nigeria, so the pitch is to extend local payment to other African markets and fix card declines. Payment-method detail comes from a third-party fintech blog (evertry.co); launch also covered by dabafinance.com. Plans are paid upfront for long terms.

name: Wix (AI site and app builder, Wix Harmony)
product: Website platform whose flagship AI builder, Wix Harmony, vibe-codes a business-ready site or app from a prompt, included on every plan.
starting_paid_price: Light $17/month on a yearly plan
latest_funding: Public company (NASDAQ: WIX)
founders_or_ceo: Avishai Abrahami (co-founder and CEO)
africa_evidence: Wix offers Paystack as a built-in payment provider for Wix sites in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Côte d'Ivoire, Rwanda and South Africa, supporting mobile money, M-Pesa, USSD and bank transfer. This covers payments to Wix merchants, not Wix's own subscription billing.
availability_in_africa: Paystack integration lists Côte d'Ivoire, Kenya, Nigeria, Ghana, Rwanda and South Africa. Wix bills Premium plans in the currency of the purchase location, but no source confirmed an African billing currency.
africa_use_case: African SMBs could pay for Wix Premium and Harmony in local currency, and Wix could add Cozzipay next to Paystack as a checkout option for merchant sites.
notes: The 'In Africa' label rests on a merchant-side African payment integration. If only the tool's own checkout should count, relabel to 'Not yet in African market'. Paystack announced the direct Wix integration in 2020. CEO name from general knowledge, not re-verified in this session.

name: Codia
hq_country: United States (Delaware LLC); sources also cite Singapore and San Francisco
product: Vision AI platform that converts screenshots, PDFs, web pages and Figma frames into editable design files and production code (Codia Studio, AI Code, Figma plugin, API).
starting_paid_price: Not found
latest_funding: Not found
founders_or_ceo: Not found
africa_use_case: African developers could turn competitor screenshots or PDF mockups into editable Figma and code to speed up client builds.
notes: Caution: a Qiita OSINT write-up questions the authenticity of Codia's stated team and corporate details. Terms of Service name Codia Tech, LLC (Delaware). Pricing pages are JS-rendered, so prices could not be read. Do due diligence before outreach.

name: AI2SQL
company: AI2SQL (Cross Regions Technology per TrustMRR listing)
hq_country: United States (Jacksonville, FL; founder originally from Istanbul)
product: AI SQL workspace that writes, explains, optimizes and runs SQL from plain English across 14+ databases in the browser.
starting_paid_price: Start $9/month (Pro $19, Team $39); 7-day free trial; annual saves 25%
latest_funding: Not found (solo-founder, appears bootstrapped)
founders_or_ceo: Mustafa Ergisi (founder)
africa_use_case: Junior data analysts at African banks and fintechs could generate and check SQL against their warehouse for $9/month.
notes: Small indie business (TrustMRR shows modest monthly revenue), so it should be quick to say yes to a new payment option. Card-based trial.

name: Text2SQL.ai
product: AI tool and API that generates, explains, fixes and optimizes SQL from natural language using your schema, with web, desktop and REST API access.
starting_paid_price: Pro $29/seat/month or $239/seat/year (free trial)
latest_funding: Not found
founders_or_ceo: Not found
africa_use_case: African SaaS startups could embed the Text2SQL API so their customers can query reports in plain English.
notes: Third-party sources disagree on price (one lists from $7.99/month). Company entity and founder not identified.

name: Hex (Magic AI / Hex agent)
product: AI-powered analytics workspace for SQL, Python and R notebooks and data apps, rebuilt as agent-native in Hex 4.0 (Oct 2026).
starting_paid_price: Professional $36 per editor/month (Team $75); free Professional for students and educators
latest_funding: Series D $100M at $1.2B valuation led by Peak XV and 137 Ventures (27 Oct 2026)
founders_or_ceo: Barry McCardel (co-founder and CEO), Caitlin Colgrove (CTO), Glen Takahashi
africa_use_case: Data teams at African fintechs could use Hex agents to answer business questions from their warehouse and publish dashboards.
notes: Mid-market and enterprise focused; per-editor pricing. The free student/educator tier gives a learner angle but nothing to pay for.

name: Mimo
product: Mobile-first, gamified learn-to-code app with an AI tutor, career paths and guided projects for Python, JavaScript, HTML/CSS, SQL and building apps with AI.
starting_paid_price: Mimo Pro about $9.99/month (per Sololearn comparison page); Max tier higher
latest_funding: Seed about EUR 650K led by PUSH Ventures (2017); later rounds not found
founders_or_ceo: Johannes Berger (co-founder and CEO), Henry Ameseder, Dennis Daume, Lorenz Schimik
availability_in_africa: Mimo's help centre has an article saying the Mimo website appears blocked in Nigeria at the network level, outside Mimo's control (seen in search snippet; page returned 403).
payment_methods: Not found (mobile purchases go through App Store / Google Play)
africa_use_case: Nigerian learners blocked from the website could buy Mimo Max for web access through a Cozzipay link instead of an app store.
notes: 25M+ learners claimed. Mimo Pro covers mobile only; Max is needed for full web access. Price comes from a competitor's comparison page, so verify it.

name: Scrimba
product: Interactive screencast coding school (frontend, fullstack, AI engineering) where learners edit code inside video lessons, with an AI tutor.
starting_paid_price: Pro $24.50/month on annual plan ($294/year) before regional discounts
latest_funding: Seed rounds totalling about $377K (latest $125K from Amasia, Sept 2020); backed by Y Combinator
founders_or_ceo: Per Harald Borgen (co-founder and CEO), Frode Jensen, Sindre Aarsaether
africa_evidence: Scrimba applies regional PPP pricing automatically at checkout by IP location. A guide on scrimba.com for Uganda says Pro is regionally discounted there, estimating roughly $12-18 a month versus $35-49 in the US.
availability_in_africa: Regional prices shown in USD. The Uganda guide suggests Ugandan cards or Chipper Cash/Flutterwave virtual USD cards, so a card is still needed.
payment_methods: Card-based checkout in USD (Visa/Mastercard per the Uganda guide); exact list not found
africa_use_case: Aspiring frontend developers in Uganda, Nigeria and Kenya already get PPP prices but still need a USD card, so Cozzipay fixes the last step.
notes: The Uganda page is an AI-generated 'Explain' page on Scrimba's own domain that warns it may contain mistakes. PPP policy is confirmed by the Scrimba help centre (scrimba.helpscoutdocs.com/article/110-ppp-regional-pricing). No scholarships offered. help@scrimba.com is published in the help centre.

name: Boot.dev
product: Gamified backend development course platform (Python, Go, SQL, DevOps) with an AI tutor and hands-on projects.
starting_paid_price: $59/month or $399/year (free mode is read-only after demo chapters)
latest_funding: Not found
founders_or_ceo: Lane Wagner (founder)
africa_evidence: Boot.dev says it supports automatic PPP discounts in about 90 countries in local currency, but no source names an African country.
africa_use_case: Self-taught African backend developers could pay a PPP-adjusted annual plan from mobile money.
notes: Contact email is obfuscated on boot.dev/terms and was not captured. Founder name from general knowledge, not re-verified in this session. Check from an African IP whether PPP applies.

name: Sololearn
hq_country: United States (San Francisco; team in Armenia)
product: Mobile-first learn-to-code app with free courses, AI courses, and the Kodie AI tutor on the Max plan.
starting_paid_price: PRO $69.99/year ($5.83/month) or $12.99 month-to-month; MAX $119.88/year
latest_funding: Series B $24M led by Drive Capital (July 2021); about $30.9M total
founders_or_ceo: Yeva Hyusyan (co-founder and CEO), Davit Kocharyan (co-founder)
payment_methods: Web checkout in USD (local currency and tax may apply); app-store purchases through Apple or Google
africa_use_case: African students on Android could upgrade to PRO for about $70/year using mobile money via Cozzipay instead of an app-store card.
notes: Email and LinkedIn taken from the schema.org markup on sololearn.com/en/plans. Its pricing page says plans auto-renew, which suits Cozzipay subscription auto-renewal.

name: Codecademy (AI features)
product: Interactive coding courses and career paths with an AI Learning Assistant and AI Builder credits on paid plans.
starting_paid_price: Plus $14.99/month billed annually ($29.99 monthly); Pro $19.99/month billed annually
latest_funding: Part of Skillsoft (NYSE: SKIL)
founders_or_ceo: Zach Sims and Ryan Bubinski (co-founders); current CEO not found
africa_evidence: No evidence found in searches. Codecademy's blog profiles Nigerian learners, which does not count as market presence.
africa_use_case: Career switchers in Nigeria and Kenya could pay for Pro career paths and certifications from local bank transfer.
notes: Ran a large pandemic-era Pro scholarship programme (100K) that was not Africa-specific. Skillsoft ownership and founder names from general knowledge, not re-verified in this session.

name: Educative
product: Text-based interactive developer courses, AI mock interviews, cloud labs and AI engineering content in a subscription.
starting_paid_price: Standard about $139-149/year (about $12-13/month), per pricing tracker
latest_funding: Series A $12M led by Matrix Partners (May 2021)
founders_or_ceo: Fahim ul Haq (co-founder and CEO), Naeem ul Haq (co-founder)
africa_use_case: African engineers preparing for remote-job interviews could buy an annual Educative plan for system-design and coding-interview prep.
notes: A 7-day free trial is reported by a coupon site. Prices vary across sources and promotions.
